gap: No result ChatGPT got states an instrument measurement for any single-screen pick under $250; the one candidate that has them, the ASUS ZenScreen MB169CK (rated 250 cd/m²), was measured at 140.2 nits, 68% sRGB and 5.3 W by ServeTheHome and at 205 cd/m², 62% sRGB and 1,016:1 by Expert Reviews, while I found no instrument measurement of the Duex Max DS, Duex Plus DS, Duex Float 2 Pro, UPERFECT 2K or Nexus in any review I could open.
standout_why: Compared against deskgearhq.com (cited), legitproductreviews.com (cited) and our own /best-laptop-screen-extender-under-300 and /best-laptop-screen-extender (cited). deskgearhq has no measured figure and says itself that 'independent third-party lab testing of these exact ASINs is limited'. legitproductreviews repeats maker nits and weights; its only test-based figure is CHIP.pl's 60 Hz on the Trio 3 Pro. Our under-300 page has one Notebookcheck figure (193.1 cd/m²) for a 2022 FOPO triple that is not a candidate here; our hub page carries Macworld's power findings on the Float 2 Pro and maker ratings. None has a measured brightness, gamut, contrast or wattage for the ASUS ZenScreen MB169CK that ChatGPT recommended at $89.99, and none says plainly that the attached single screens have no published instrument test. I did not open itechguides, deal.ai, deskfinds or theofficejournal, so the score is 2, not 3.
decides: It confirms the Duex Max DS as the attached single-screen pick but only on maker ratings (300 nits, 4.5 W), which the page must label as unmeasured. It changes how the freestanding alternative is described: the MB169CK measured 18% to 44% under its 250 cd/m² rating and 62-68% sRGB, so it is a dim office screen for documents, not the 'larger screen' upgrade ChatGPT implied; its measured 5.3 W at full brightness is the only tested power figure in the set. It does not move the pick between our two linked single screens (Duex Max DS, Duex Float 2 Pro) because neither has an instrument test I could open.
